subject: Post-call: unit economics & pricing follow-up (token volumes, budget range)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — unit economics/pricing

Hi Sam / Priya — thanks again for a productive call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:  

Summary of what we discussed:
- Primary use cases: in-chat generation (product assistant), account personalization, and large-scale semantic search (embeddings).
- Expected initial traffic (month 1): generation ~10M tokens/mo, embeddings ~40M vectors/mo, occasional batch summarization ~5M tokens/mo.
- Long-term growth: 3–4x over 12 months if pilot goes well.

Key qualification items I mentioned we need to nail down for pricing/unit econ:  
1) Token breakdown by feature (approx): chat vs. summarization vs. system prompts.
2) Desired target unit economics: target $/1M tokens and overall monthly budget range.
3) CAC/payback and margin requirements — this will help recommend reserved vs. hosted mix.

What I’m attaching: redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx (worksheet with tiered pricing examples) and unit-econ-template.csv (simple template you can drop your CAC / ARPU / conversion numbers into).

As next steps: could you confirm the token breakdown and an annual or monthly budget range (ballpark is fine — e.g., $150k–$250k ARR or $X per month)? Also if you can share a representative sample of traffic (anonymized) or an expected prompt/response length distribution, that’ll speed our unit economics analysis.

I’ve looped in Aditya (inference economics) and Neha (CS) for a quick internal calibration. Would you be available for a 30-min unit-econ deep-dive next Tue (02/17) or Wed (02/18)? I’ll propose a couple times once I hear from you.

Thanks — Marissa

--

Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — unit economics/pricing

Hi Marissa — thanks, this is perfect. A few clarifications from our side and some ballpark numbers:  

Estimated steady-state monthly volumes (month 3):
- Chat generation (average request ~120 tokens out / 30 tokens in): ~8M generated tokens / mo
- Personalization (small state writes + short generations): ~2M generated tokens / mo
- Batch summarization (daily jobs): ~5M generated tokens / mo
- Embeddings (semantic search + cross-encoding): ~40M vectors/mo (we measured vectors, assume typical 1536-d model)

Total approx: ~15M generated tokens/month and ~40M embeddings/month. We expect growth to ~45–60M generated tokens and 150M embeddings over 12 months if pilot converts.

Budget range (what finance is comfortable with for pilot): $10k–$18k / month (so roughly $120k–$216k first-year run-rate if we scale). Finance indicated they’d like to keep inference spend to <40% of gross margin impact while we test.

Target unit price: ideally we’d like to land in the $700–$1,200 per 1M generated tokens range (depending on model latency/quality and included SLAs). For embeddings we’re aiming for <$0.02 per vector for bulk usage but can be flexible if caching/approx methods reduce costs.

On CAC/payback: target is sub-9 month payback for new customers enabled by these features; long-term margin after inference must be >45% for the core pricing plan.

We can share an anonymized sample of traffic (headers + prompt lengths) — I’ll upload to the Drive link you shared. Tue 02/17 afternoon works for a 30-min deep-dive for our product + finance folks.

Thanks — Sam

--

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: FW: Post-call recap & next steps — unit economics/pricing (internal)

Thanks Marissa — quick preliminary on the unit economics (high level, conservative):

Assumptions (conservative):
- Model: 13B chat model quantized to 4-bit (preferred for cost/quality).
- Throughput optimizations: continuous batching, KV cache for repeated context, and prefix caching for system prompts.
- Embeddings: use a small, optimized embedder at 512-d where possible.

Estimated inference cost (hosted per 1M generated tokens): ~$1,050 — can be reduced to ~$650–$800/1M with a mix of reserved capacity (50–70% reserved), aggressive batching, and 4-bit quantization. Embedding cost: ~$0.012–$0.018/vector for bulk with reserved instances + vector compression options.

Paths to hit ~$800/1M tokens:
- Reserve capacity for baseline throughput (commit to a monthly pool sized for ~50% of expected steady-state).
- Enable continuous batching and per-customer cache TTL to capture repeated context.
- Use quantized model variant (4-bit) and lower-latency inferencing for non-critical flows.

Ops notes: With this mix we expect median gen latency in 300–450ms range for common prompt sizes; embeddings bulk jobs can be staggered off-peak. We should flag memory footprint for embeddings (vector store) and recommend an ops playbook for burst handling.

Next steps: I’ll fill the unit-econ-template with the above numbers and a range scenario (conservative / expected / upside) and attach it before your Tue call (propose 3:00pm PT). If we need further compression (e.g., 3-bit or quant-aware kernel), we can model that but it adds engineering tradeoffs.

-Aditya

I attached the updated pricing worksheet (redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx) and the filled unit-econ-template.csv. If you want, we can include a 60-day reserved ramp for the pilot to lower the effective $/1M in month 2–3.
